newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer shares still rally despite rate rise.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer shares still rally despite rate rise.

text.p: Shares in brewer to leisure groups Whitbread Plc, Bass Plc, Greenalls Group Plc and Scottish and Newcastle Plc continued their strong bull run on Thursday, despite a decision by Britain's central bank to raise interest rates.

The Bank of England's decision to raise interest rates by a quarter point to 6.75 percent was viewed by economists as insufficient to dampen consumer spending and they expected a further increase in August.
"The strength of consumer demand in the year to date and the underperformance of the sector makes them look relatively good value," said Frazer Ramsan, an analyst at Lehman Brothers.

Shares in the sector began to rally shortly after Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's budget on May 2. Brown forecast consumer spending would rise by 4.5 percent this year and 4.0 percent in 1998.

Shares in Greenalls Group, owners of De Vere Hotels and holiday lodges led the pack, to stand 17-1/2p at 443p by 1225 GMT. Whitbread, owners of Marriott hotels, pub restaurant chain Brewers Fayre and French bistro-style Cafe Rouge and Cafe Dome saw its shares rise 16-1/2p to 784p.
Britain's largest brewer Scottish and Newcastle Plc, owners of holiday camps Center Parcs, gained 8p to 784p while Bass Plc was 10-1/2p higher at 793p.
